title: Jelly Roll's band and Leake's Lake pavilion
summary: Two years with Jelly's six-piece band; Clem's attempt to rent Leake's Lake, a big dance pavilion in Watts.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: Yeah. Did you join Jelly Roll in playing in a band or anything with him ever? Did you ever play with him?

Oh, yes. Yeah, I mentioned that. I was with him for two years when he decided to organize a band. And we went from town to town to play. And we played around Los Angeles and various places. We were, as a band of six of us. We were trying to operate a place. It was called Leakes Lake.
Oh, yeah. That was down in Watts, wasn't it?
And I went down there. Where was it? Can you remember about what part?
No, I wouldn't remember. I even had papers and everything for that place because I was trying to buy it by paying rent for it. And the rent was, but it wasn't successful.
Well, what was Leakes Lake? Was it really a lake or a resort?
A big pavilion, a big pavilion. See, in any place you wanted to have something like a big gathering, it would go to Leakes Lake. That's the only place available at that time.
Was it really a lake or anything there?

No, a big dry place, but they named it Leakes Lake. And someone told me when it used to rain so hard and everything get flooded, it was like a lake, so they named it Leakes Lake. Oh. But it was a great big pavilion.
Where did you get the Leakes part? Was that the name of the man that owned it or something?
Well, I couldn't recall that either, no.
You know, it's funny. It was a big dance pavilion.
Was there a ground there for picnics and theaters?

Well, yes. No one seemed to keep it up at that time. They had little tables built out there, but no grass or nothing. People would sit out there and have their lunch. And summertime would be so hot around there. They'd sit out and drink beer. They had those tables built on the ground. Yeah. Yeah.
